summary: In this fiction excerpt, the narrator Morgan tells her hospitalized uncle Lou that she will travel to a Third World country to find Alex Goddard, a colonel who she believes has taken Yuki and hidden her there. Lou warns her the place is dangerous and suggests alerting the embassy instead, but Morgan refuses, and Lou is sedated. Morgan plans to call Steve, who is in Belize, and a doctor then arrives to check on Lou, who will stay for observation for a couple of days.
one_line: Morgan resolves to travel abroad to find Yuki and Colonel Alex Goddard despite her uncle Lou's warnings, while Lou recovers in hospital.
key_facts: Morgan tells Lou that she is going to a Third World country to locate Alex Goddard.
Lou warns Morgan that getting crossways with the rule-makers down there is a seriously wrong thing to do.
Lou suggests alerting the embassy to have them start looking for the missing woman.
Morgan is absolutely sure that Ramos has taken Yuki.
Yuki sends a message reading "I'm lactose intolerant" and nothing more.
Ramos is described as a "diplomat" who could easily fudge the passport formalities.
Morgan plans to call Steve the minute she gets home, though Steve is in Belize and maybe not even reachable.
Morgan says Sarah and Ramos might even be on the same plane as her.
The nurses give Lou a sedative after he is moved to a gurney and his room is ready.
Dr. M. Summers, a middle-aged WASP with dark hair and slightly balding, checks Lou's chart and pulse.
Lou is told he will stay in hospital for a couple of days for observation.
Dr. Summers calls Lou "Mr. . . . Crenshaw" and tells him he is a lucky man.
Morgan thinks Lou's warning about Alex Goddard is 'an exceptionally lousy thought process' as Lou says it.
